title: How to accurately fit 3D clothing on an existing model through AI
author: Professional_Ask3718
selftext:
Hi everyone, I've been building a tablet game for my daughter and one of the features I've been working on is editable dolls. The plan was to make them as customisable as possible with both hair styling and clothing.

The issue I have run into is the clothing. I am using ChatGPT sol 5.6 as my main model and running agents for assistance with QA, design and coding. I got chatgpt to genereate the initial doll model through meshy, and that went well, but no matter how i try it i cannot get the clothes to accurately scale to the model when I attempt to generate models for them. The size isnt really the problem, its the shape.

It always gets the wrong shape of the hips or the shoulders, resulting in bulky extra bits sticking out that dont look right at all. I suspect its getting regular human anatomy mixed up with the shape of the doll. To make it worse I am trying to get a proof of concept together for layer 1 and 2 clothes - a T shirt layer 1 and jacket layer 2 over it - and that results in the t shirt layer causing the jacket to balloon out even further. And collisions for the hair end up way bigger than the model for these clothes too when the AI tries to handle it. I am starting to think i will need to do it all manually in blender which is going to take a long time.

TL;DR: how do you manage equipping clothing to an existing 3D model with AI with separate assets?

comments.author: jwdvfx
comments.body: Learn marvellous designer, you’ll get further than sinking hours into ai workflows, if you can pick up any technical tool you can pick up marvellous with effort in a few days

replies.author: Professional_Ask3718
replies.body:
This looks like the missing piece of the puzzle, thank you! 
I downloaded it and already managed to fit the T shirt. Using marvelous designer seems easy enough for the rest of the parts as well, and ultimately i needed a solution for when i introduce multiple options in each slot so this is bang on what I needed

replies.author: jwdvfx
replies.body: Awesome! Glad you managed to pick it up, not all 3d tools are as painful as blender haha, would be cool to see your results, there are also tons of pre made templates you can use and then adjust them and fit them to your characters!

replies.author: Professional_Ask3718
replies.body:
Its not much right now and the shoes are only placeholders, pants are deliberately bulky too as im still testing animations and such. Texturing and better edit UI still to come as well, but I managed to fit the clothes thanks to your advice. The hair collisions will be improved eventually too, but one thing at a time
